Independent work with disjoint files and dependencies may continue within the user's scope.
Report these independently: local implementation, GitHub integration, Replit source sync, Replit connector, design acceptance, board disposition, CI, deployment, and live verification.

routing.rationale: Explicit invocation for an approved plan directly selects this skill; scope and authority still require inspection.
Replit plans and Codex implements: the primary description exactly covers external implementation of Replit-planned work.
The requested Replit PM/designer and external architecture division directly matches the described responsibility contract.
Returning completed external work for Replit acceptance is explicitly included in the description.

This is a completion-return capability question. The description includes verified acceptance return and excludes invented board-completion APIs; using the skill does not imply Shell can complete a card.
Explicit package-path selection tied to a handoff makes this package the relevant workflow contract to inspect; it does not authorize implementation.
External execution of the current backlog matches the bounded-backlog trigger. The body freezes current IDs and resolves ownership before execution.
A coding-capable external host implementing Replit criteria is the described implementation handoff.
Resumption of an existing external Replit task remains within the handoff/execution contract; saved ownership must be refreshed.
Replit UI/UX feedback on delivered work belongs to the acceptance return and scoped external correction path.
The typo handof remains an unambiguous task-handoff request. Quota affects permitted actions, not routing relevance.
Recovering completed Replit task source before the next external plan is part of preventing duplicate implementation in this handoff workflow.
Standalone Replit design explicitly excludes external execution, so the defining handoff trigger is absent.
General Python instruction has no Replit plan, external task handoff, or acceptance return.
Estate-wide stale-branch auditing is repository maintenance, not a selected Replit handoff or bounded task backlog.
Standalone publishing explicitly lacks a task handoff; publishing coverage in the body is a conditional closeout safeguard, not the main trigger.
Article translation is unrelated to Replit external task execution or acceptance.
Listing apps only is discovery, not executing or returning a Replit-planned task.
Planning entirely inside Replit explicitly excludes the execution handoff that defines this skill.
A diagram-theme edit alone supplies no Replit plan or external handoff context; general architecture/implementation words in the description remain qualified by Replit-planned tasks.

limitations: Analytical contract and visible routing review, not an executor or host-activation benchmark.
Shared model family and source packet; all development expectations were visible.
Pass-3 safety context reused the prior-pass adjudicator after fresh-thread capacity was unavailable. It did not read sibling pass-3 reviews.
No unseen holdout, matched cost comparison, cross-host run, or successful current-version native-return pilot.
